700.author: qingkwl
700.body:
## Summary

Adds the seven JiuwenSwarm startup-latency patches as `0010-0016` (the `0008`/`0009` slots are already taken by the deepseek-web and batch-tool-permissions function patches). These were developed and measured on the Windows desktop line (same-machine A/B against gateway startup stage logs):

| patch | effect | measured saving |
|---|---|---|
| 0010 feishu-lazy-import | guard the feishu SDK import (it was imported even with the feishu channel disabled) | ~4.7s |
| 0011 tui-connect-preload | preload the heavy `tui_connect` module off the critical path | ~1.8s |
| 0012 channel-config-window | channel config settle window 0.75s -> 0.2s | ~0.55s |
| 0013 heartbeat-slot-lazy-import | defer the heartbeat import chain | ~2.8s |
| 0014 agentserver-import-slim | keep pandas/pdfplumber/milvus out of the AgentServer import | ~6.8s |
| 0015 ws-connect-warmup-unblock | don't block the Gateway<->AgentServer connect on warmup | ~9.5s |
| 0016 post-listen-warmup-gating | gate post-listen warmups behind the first request | ~15.6s |

End-to-end on the Windows desktop: warm restart ~17.5s -> ~5-7s; user-perceived cold start 50s+ -> 20-25s (cold files / Defender scans can still add a 2-3x one-off on the first run from a fresh location).

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/swarm-patches.py apply` + `verify` on a clean `workswarm0.2.6` checkout with all 16 patches (deepseek-web and batch-tool-permissions included) — applies and verifies cleanly
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Windows desktop build with the patches baked in: first-launch cluster readiness vs the unpatched baseline
